record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.original_question: In the planar case of tensegrities on 10 labeled points, describe every possible type of stratum that can occur in the configuration-space stratification by sign-preserving equivalence classes of self-stress fibers.

evidence.quote: A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
The next case which contains unknown strata is n = 10 (see also Problem 8 below). Problem 2 Describe all the possible different types of strata for 10 points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and edge set $E$. A tensegrity framework realizing $G$ in the plane is a configuration $p=(p_1,\dots,p_n)\in(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$ together with the straight-line edges $\overline{p_ip_j}$ for $\{i,j\}\in E$. A self-stress on $(G,p)$ is an assignment $w:E\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for every vertex $i$,
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
The set of self-stresses forms a real vector space $W(G,p)$, called the self-stress fiber at $p$. Fix the graph $G$ and consider the configuration space $\mathcal{C}(G)=(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$ minus the locus where the dimension of $W(G,p)$ jumps; on its open part $B_d(G)$ where $\dim W(G,p)=d$, declare two configurations $p,q$ equivalent if there is a linear isomorphism $W(G,p)\to W(G,q)$ that preserves the sign of every edge weight (sign-preserving equivalence of fibers). A stratum is a maximal connected component of $B_d(G)$ consisting of configurations all of which are mutually equivalent in this sense.

Problem. For $n=10$ labeled points in the plane, describe every possible type of stratum that can arise in this stratification, ranging over all graphs $G$ on $10$ vertices.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in Karpenkov's list of open problems on configuration spaces of tensegrities (Arnold Math. J., 2018), where $n=10$ is identified as the smallest case still containing unknown strata. No subsequent classification of all 10-point planar tensegrity strata was found in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: The next case which contains unknown strata is n = 10. Problem 2: Describe all the possible different types of strata for 10 points.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of strata for 10-point planar tensegrities is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.snippet: Stratification of configuration spaces of tensegrities by sign-preserving equivalence of self-stress fibers.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework of strata used in the problem; smaller n are studied but n=10 is not classified.
